issues: Matthew Alderson-Jenner reported Maki Nori sales of £14.6K last week with wages at 49.41%, which Michael Salvador called awful (Admin Meeting 26/10).
Covers fell by 123 week on week and spend per head fell by £1.68.

Teddy Lee said Maki Nori currently loses more money open than it would closed, and that from next week it will close on Mondays and Tuesdays, to be discussed with Ginger and Ziang Lin (Admin Meeting 26/10).

Teddy Lee linked the Maki Nori plan to Soho needing more space, and asked Ziang Lin to fix Maki Nori first, measuring and confirming the layout and bar plan; council approval is needed for outside changes (Admin Meeting 26/10).
Successes this week: service and more training, store management, communication, food presentation and the specials, especially the soup.
Areas for improvement: service standards, compliance, upselling and cleaning.
Some bad reviews were received this week, and reviews need to improve.
Staffing: Beverly is fully integrated with the team, the team is still being finalised, and Victorija is to be trained in costs.
Hygiene checks were at 100% compliance, and all waste was tracked.
Cleanliness is being worked on day by day, with a lot of FOH and BOH cleaning this week and a deep clean arranged for the coming days.
Pest control is being monitored constantly.
Maintenance: there is a leak in the KP area.
Upcoming: Omakase nights on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, and the lunch promo.
Lunch promo marketing materials are on the tables and posters are in the window; the new Omakase material is not ready yet.
Region (London KPI meeting 27/10): managers must move from the manual KPI sheets to the automated admin dashboard, which tracks cleaning checklists, delivery metrics and food costs.
Region (London KPI meeting 27/10): Ross Ward showed how to customise the weekly Mapal tasks with specific instructions so they are done consistently.
Region (London KPI meeting 27/10): accurate stock counts and correct invoice recording in Kobas are needed to stop the data being inflated.
Region (London KPI meeting 27/10): managers must use the formal maintenance logs to report issues.
Ziang Lin reviewed Maki Nori's week: spend per head was about £40 and reviews were positive 4 and 5 stars (London KPI meeting 27/10).

Monday and Tuesday closures for renovation are planned with about three weeks of lead time; details stay confidential until official dates are released, and the closure will be framed around improving the upstairs (London KPI meeting 27/10).

Renovation plan: extend the full bar to the window with a double or triple door glass fridge, glass washer and cocktail station, remove the window seating and Sakura, give a large section to sushi and convert the bin room for beer kegs and draught Coca Cola; Ziang Lin preferred this to Michael's layout (London KPI meeting 27/10).

Downstairs: remove the middle area, fit darker non wood flooring, fix the ceiling leaks, add emergency lighting and storage racking, and move the ice machine and a corner freezer downstairs; the sushi prep area becomes a waiting and drinks storage station (London KPI meeting 27/10).

Operating plan: keep labour at 20% to 25% by running weekday lunch upstairs (up to about £5,000) and sending food down by lift if needed, cutting downstairs labour by about 70%, and open both kitchens for busy evenings and weekend dinners (London KPI meeting 27/10).
A phased workforce transition plan for the Maki Nori to Maki Ramen conversion was agreed, covering the roles to fill and the recruitment gaps (AM Updates 28/10).
Region (London KPI meeting 27/10): daily report submissions are still mandatory alongside the automated admin dashboard.

Region (London KPI meeting 27/10): stock edit access is suspended for all sites for one to two weeks to show true variances, after some head chefs used stock edits to add waste and balance variances (35 broth wastes a week against 130 uses); adding false waste is prohibited.
Region (London KPI meeting 27/10): GMs must reply constructively to 1 star reviews and offer the customer a free meal to win them back.
Region (London KPI meeting 27/10): cross site shift cover, such as staff borrowed between Shoreditch, Soho and Lakeside, must be logged in the dashboard's covers tool.
